review.label: sha256-053b282c2890f71eb9a9f07de2957faa54161febe88a8a11aee53d9f923d625b
review.rationale: The code concretely performs whole-recipe rewrite passes over instructions and equipment. Nevertheless, `_sections` is only a traversal abstraction, not a dependency representation: no ingredient identity/index points to the instructions or equipment that reference it. Global substring replacement does not satisfy reference awareness.

citations.explanation: This operation globally rewrites every collected main/component instruction list.
A substitution updates the ingredient and then propagates wording and equipment effects outside its row.

review.label: sha256-40441174311594509bffefaf39b84b23753adb2c51d3fe657040c639c990efd4
review.rationale: The shared instruction-list collection enables a global rewrite pass, but there is no explicit identity/index link between an ingredient and the instructions or equipment that depend on it. Every wording change is applied indiscriminately to every instruction list, and ingredient IDs are not used. The required reference-aware mechanism is absent.

review.label: sha256-48ed005f2141d0f8ba135355d675b1fbc58deb84017d16c54c5217b1662c998b
review.rationale: The implementation performs ordered whole-recipe wording and equipment rewrites, but it does not build or preserve any ingredient-to-instruction/equipment reference or semantic link. Ingredient IDs are never used to identify dependent fields; wording is unscoped global string replacement. Therefore the reference-aware requirement and frozen correspondence are not fully instantiated.

citations.explanation: Successful substitution chains commit ordered wording effects and equipment changes beyond the ingredient row.
Committed wording effects are applied in order to component and main recipe instructions.

review.label: sha256-58faf13efb81196cfe796ea59f0bddeaf99678b8557063135033cdde55b58e24
review.rationale: Buffered substitution effects form an ordered global rewrite, but the buffer is not reference-aware: it has no mapping from ingredient identity to the instruction or equipment fields dependent on that ingredient. Ingredient IDs only populate output records, while wording changes are blanket replacements. The full frozen mechanism therefore fails.

citations.explanation: Substitution effects are accumulated in ordered shared wording and equipment collections.
The ordered changes are subsequently applied to recipe and component instruction strings.

review.label: sha256-7cbf972a41e4deb877aabd5dcb97a8e38ad0de3303c462fc65589f9a753fba31
review.rationale: The context provides ordered cross-field effects and global rewriting, but it is not a reference-aware intermediate representation: it contains no mapping from ingredient identity to dependent instruction or equipment fields. Replacements operate by unrestricted text matching, so evidence item 1 and the frozen correspondence fail.

citations.explanation: Substitution processing records ordered wording and equipment effects in shared state.
The ordered wording effects are replayed across complete instruction lists.

review.label: sha256-ac815a4db03c053dd6bb33dcef8f86f07f78d064600f195ac69c0fcb22e715d8
review.rationale: `_State` coordinates ordered cross-cutting rewrites, but it contains no reference from an ingredient identity to dependent instruction/equipment fields. Ingredient IDs are copied into rows only; `_reword` applies every change to every line. This is a global rewrite but not the required reference-aware transformation.

citations.explanation: A substitution accumulates wording and equipment effects in shared whole-recipe state.
Those ordered effects are later applied to top-level and component instruction strings.

review.label: sha256-af3523520a43be4fea7c649dcf4df344c3511e0a71a25a83c65dd0013b0b9c9c
review.rationale: The implementation has ordered global propagation to instructions and equipment, but no ingredient-reference graph, index, or semantic link connects a substitution to its dependents. Its IDs never participate in rewrite targeting, and all wording changes are applied indiscriminately across every instruction.

citations.explanation: Each substitution queues ordered wording edits and directly alters shared equipment state.
The queued edits are applied across main and component instruction lists.

review.label: sha256-b1f95c231498237d8d85a7556d8cbebf3c48637a41141d98639627d6b10db85d
review.rationale: Substitutions cause ordered global changes to instructions and equipment, satisfying the propagation requirement. However, there is no ingredient-identity reference, dependency index, or semantic representation linking a changed ingredient to particular dependent fields. IDs remain inert and text edits are globally applied, so the full mechanism is not present.

citations.explanation: A substitution immediately applies each wording change over the entire copied instruction list and updates shared equipment.

review.label: sha256-ebeb370391b4a5830ec1df68273231fafbc0e677a20adc813f28dc3abb0b436f
review.rationale: There is a whole-list instruction/equipment rewrite, but it is not reference-aware. No ingredient identity is linked to dependent instructions or equipment, components are not included in rewriting, and IDs are only copied into output rows. Thus the required reference/index mechanism and frozen correspondence are absent.
